plain: A researcher, Geoffrey Drumm (also listed as Jeffrey), says on Jesse Michels's podcast in 2026 that the Giza Plateau, the high ground in Egypt where the great pyramids stand, was once the bottom of an ancient ocean from millions of years ago called the Tethys Sea. He says that seabed would have had hydrothermal vents, openings where hot, mineral-rich water rises from below. In one telling he links these vents to vertical columns that a team led by a man named Filippo found in radar scans under the pyramids, and he places a chamber of molten rock, or magma, beneath them. If true, it would mean the pyramids sit on top of a natural source of heat and energy, which fits the episode's claim of an energy grid under Giza.
